definitions.explanation: While something is happening; at the peak of an activity.

examples.japanese: {会議|かいぎ}の{最中|さいちゅう}に
examples.english: In the middle of a meeting.

examples.japanese: {食事|しょくじ}の{最中|さいちゅう}
{仕事|しごと}の{最中|さいちゅう}に{電話|でんわ}がかかってきた。
examples.english: A phone call came in the middle of work.

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}の{最中|さいちゅう}に{地震|じしん}が{起|お}きて、{全員|ぜんいん}が{避難|ひなん}した。
examples.english: An earthquake occurred during the exam, and everyone evacuated.

examples.japanese: {友達|ともだち}と{電話|でんわ}で{話|はな}している{最中|さいちゅう}に、{急|きゅう}にバッテリーが{切|き}れてしまった。
examples.english: While I was talking on the phone with a friend, the battery suddenly died.

notes:
{最中|さいちゅう} means "in the very middle of" an activity or event. It emphasizes that the action is actively in progress at that moment.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- Noun + の{最中|さいちゅう}に: {会議|かいぎ}の{最中|さいちゅう}に (in the middle of a meeting)
- Verb ている + {最中|さいちゅう}に: {話|はな}している{最中|さいちゅう}に (while talking)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {最中|さいちゅう}: right in the middle of (emphasizes the peak of activity)
- {途中|とちゅう}: midway through, on the way (emphasizes being partway through)
- {間|あいだ}に: during (more general time frame)

CAUTION:
Do not confuse with {最中|もなか}, a completely different word meaning a traditional Japanese wafer sweet filled with bean paste.

REGISTER:
Slightly formal. In casual speech, ～している{時|とき}に is more natural.
